To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the mean-variance efficient frontier of the UK financial market is well defined; (ii) investors hold mean-variance optimal portfolios; (iii) the risk-return trade-offs are not constant; (iv) the risk aversion of investors increases with their wealth; (v) investors are willing to pay a premium for portfolio insurance, and (vi) the general non-availability of portfolio insurance is due to the lack of supply rather than the lack of demand.
(1) The mean-variance efficiency of the portfolios of financial assets held by U.K. investors is not significantly different from zero.
(i) the mean-variance efficient portfolio of financial assets is a reasonable approximation for the portfolio actually held by investors and (ii) investors are risk averse.
